lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Let's run jobs as real users.
At your site, jobs run as real users, under Slurm accounts with limits. How do you test that on a cluster where root does everything?
Here's the example. A db node keeps the accounts, and the slurm section turns on enforcement of associations and limits.
physics, the parent account, caps its jobs at four CPUs together. Its child, theory, allows only one running job per user.
alice, bob and carol get Slurm accounts, and two of them get roles: coordinator and operator. dave gets none.
Every node gets the users and groups with the same IDs, and each user a home on the shared home volume.
Once slurmctld has registered the cluster, sind creates this account tree with sacctmgr.
So this cluster tests your limits: alice gets one job at a time, and physics stops at four CPUs, out of six.
dave has no association, so his sbatch is rejected outright.
To act as a user, log in with sind ssh and a user name, or pass the user flag to sind exec or sind enter.
The identity mode decides which nodes have the Linux accounts. local, the default, puts them on every node.
With nssSlurm, the workers don't have them, and with clientIds, only the login node does. Pick the one your site runs.
So: declare users and accounts in the config, turn on enforcement, and mirror the identity mode of your site.
Next up, the design overview. See you there!
